title: Elementary functions and logarithms: the platform libm on doubles
verdict: sqrt correctly rounded; macOS: tan 2.4 ulp, log(b, x) 1.4 ulp, the rest < 1 ulp; Linux: glibc's bounds
description: Each function is one `<cmath>` call on `double` (`std::sqrt`, `std::exp`, `std::log`, `std::log10`, `std::log2`, `std::pow`, `std::sin`, …): the platform's libm, so every bound but sqrt's is platform-dependent. `log(b, x)` is `log10(x) / log10(b)`: two libm calls and a division. `pow` has no shortcuts. A FLOAT argument widens exactly to DOUBLE and the result is DOUBLE (duckdb-float-math-double), so an fp32 input gets the fp64 libm answer.

Max error in ulps of the DOUBLE result, measured on macOS arm64 (3 000 inputs each, fp64 inputs / FLOAT inputs widened): sqrt 0.5 / 0.5 (correctly rounded on every platform); exp 0.502 / 0.504; ln 0.500 / 0.500; log10 0.500 / 0.498; log2 0.502 / 0.498; log(b, x) 1.42 / 1.44; pow 0.504 / 0.503 (also with integer exponents 2 to 9: ≤ 0.505); sin 0.77 / 0.62; cos 0.83 / 0.77; tan 2.30 / 2.40; asin 0.61 / 0.61; acos 0.89 / 0.89; atan 0.72 / 0.64; atan2 0.56 / 0.51.

tan exceeds 1 ulp on macOS: 1 252 of 3 000 results miss the correctly rounded value, at moderate arguments too, e.g. tan(1.0391439199447632) = 1.7002787929535204 where the correctly rounded value is 1.7002787929535208 (1.9 ulp). log(b, x) misses on a quarter of the inputs. ln, log10 and log2 were correctly rounded on every probed input but log2 once (0.502); exp, pow, atan2 within 0.51.

Cast back to FLOAT, every FLOAT-input result above was within 0.5 ulp of binary32 (0 off the correctly rounded binary32 value for each function): the extra rounding from DOUBLE to FLOAT can only matter when the DOUBLE lies within its own error of a binary32 midpoint.

Linux x86_64 (glibc, version unknown; the bounds are the glibc 2.39 manual's): exp, ln, sin, cos, asin, acos, atan, pow 1 ulp; log10, log2 2 ulp; atan2, tan, sqrt no known error; log(b, x) then about 2 · 2 + 0.5 ulp by its formula. To be measured on homelab.

Linux x86_64 (glibc 2.39), same 3000 inputs per function: most functions are within about 0.5 ulp where macOS is not (sin 0.50 against 0.77, acos 0.50 against 0.89, tan at moderate arguments 0.51 against 2.4), but `cos` and `tan` of DOUBLE reach 7.95 and 14.36 ulp at x = 5.319372648326541e+255, near a zero of `cos` (glibc gives cos = -4.68716592425462e-19, the exact value is -4.6871659242546276e-19; macOS is within 0.05 ulp there, checked with mpmath at 3000 bits). `log10` reaches 1.35 ulp on Linux (0.50 on macOS) and `log(b, x)` 1.47 to 1.56. So no libm-backed function has a platform-independent bound below glibc's: take the larger of the two columns, and more for huge arguments of `cos` and `tan`.

The docs are silent on the math functions' accuracy: a docs gap. No upstream test pins this, and none can, since DuckDB's sqllogictests compare floating results within 1 %; it may change between versions.
reference: The reference computes these with Lean's `Float`, which calls the same platform libm, and fixes `rounding: TIE_TO_EVEN`; the core leaves the last bits to each engine (#54). sverify's ε for a function is the engine's bound on the platform it runs on (#85), so the ε table needs a column per platform.

evidence.note: pow: std::pow, a raise for 0 to a negative power unless ieee_floating_point_ops
ln, log10, log2: std::log, std::log10, std::log2
sin, cos, tan, asin, atan, atan2, acos: std:: on double

glibc 2.39 manual, table 'Known Maximum Errors in Math Functions', x86_64 column, in ulps: double acos 1, asin 1, atan 1, atan2 -, cos 1, exp 1, log 1, log10 2, log2 2, pow 1, sin 1, sqrt -, tan -; float acosf 1, asinf 1, atanf 1, atan2f 2, cosf 1, expf 1, logf 1, log10f 2, log2f 1, powf 1, sinf 1, sqrtf -, tanf 1. '-' is no known error beyond correct rounding.

The current manual drops the table: glibc aims at results 'within a few ulp' and correct rounding only for sqrt, fma, rint and string conversions; its test suite flags errors above 9 ulp. The numbers are the largest errors glibc's tests have found, not proved bounds.

provenance.notes: For the Linux x86_64 column. The glibc version on a given Linux machine is unknown here (`ldd --version` gives it); the 2.39 table is the last that lists x86_64. macOS's libm documents no error bounds (the SDK's man pages for sin, tan, log, pow state special values only), so the macOS column rests on the probe.

evidence.sql: SELECT sqrt(x), exp(x), ln(x), log10(x), log2(x), sin(x), cos(x), tan(x), asin(x), acos(x), atan(x) FROM t  -- t(x DOUBLE), one function per run on its own inputs
SELECT atan2(a, b), pow(a, b), log(a, b) FROM t  -- t(a DOUBLE, b DOUBLE)
SELECT pow(x, n) FROM t  -- n = 2 … 9, x in ±[0.5, 2]
evidence.observed: max 0.4994 to 0.5053 ulp; at most 5 of 3 000 off

evidence.sql: the same functions on t(x FLOAT)
evidence.observed: DOUBLE results: sqrt 0.5, exp 0.5036, ln 0.4999, log10 0.4977, log2 0.4984, sin 0.6240, cos 0.7690, tan 2.4028 (958 of 2 323), asin 0.6122, acos 0.8898, atan 0.6414, atan2 0.5104, pow 0.5030, log(b, x) 1.4368; CAST(… AS FLOAT) of each ≤ 0.5000 ulp of binary32, 0 off
1.7002787929535204 (mpmath: 1.70027879295352078…, correctly rounded 1.7002787929535208); the same from Python's math.tan and libSystem's tan via ctypes

notes: Probe script ulp_probe.py (session scratchpad, not in the repository), run from python/ as `uv run --with mpmath python ulp_probe.py --n 3000 --seed 1 --out ulp.json`: about 3 000 inputs per operation and type, random and hard cases, against mpmath at 256 bits. 'bad' counts results that differ from the correctly rounded value; the max is in ulps of the result type at the exact value's binade. DuckDB runs on a table loaded from Parquet, Polars on a LazyFrame with collect(engine='streaming'), so the column kernels run. DuckDB 2.0.0 and Polars 2.1.0 (Python wheels), macOS 26.6 arm64, Python 3.12.11, mpmath 1.3.0.

Hard cases included: ln, log10, log2 at 1 ± k·2^-52 and 1 ± 1e-6; sin, cos, tan at multiples of π/2 ± 1e-6, at |x| up to 1e308 (1e22, 6381956970095103·2^797); asin, acos near 0.5 and ±1; exp near 0 and up to ±700.

provenance.checked_by: characterization pipeline platform run (homelab, Linux x86_64, glibc 2.39-0ubuntu8.9; scratchpad ulp_probe.py --n 3000 --seed 1, the same inputs as the macOS run)
